headline: Clerk at District Court Error-Checking Office Receives 'Notice of Receipt of His Own Notice' Regarding Unpaid Tea Bill
body:
Ramesh Kumar, a low-level filing clerk at the District Court, spent four hours on Tuesday morning drafting a formal notice to himself after he accidentally filed his own canteen expense claim in the ‘State Secrecy’ department. The clerical error, which triggered an automated legal notification sequence, resulted in Kumar receiving a registered courier package containing a legal notice addressed to him, by him, regarding a pending balance of 42 rupees for samosas consumed during the monsoon session.

“I was honestly impressed by the efficiency of our own department,” said Kumar, while reviewing the sixteen-page document that outlined the potential consequences of ignoring a demand notice he had typed out himself. “The paperwork is bulletproof, the citations are impeccable, and the deadline for me to respond to my own request is tomorrow by 5:00 PM. I am currently debating whether to file an extension on my own behalf or simply settle the matter with the canteen owner before the ‘State Secrecy’ team decides to escalate the case to the High Court.”

Legal analysts suggest this is a historic milestone for local bureaucracy, as it marks the first time a single civil servant has successfully managed to keep an entire legal proceedings cycle contained within his own cubicle. “It’s about streamlining,” added a supervisor from the nearby registry office. “If everyone in the building started sending notices to themselves instead of filing them against random celebrities or ministers, we would clear the current backlog of cases by the end of the fiscal year.”
caption: Efficiency is just a notice away, especially when you're the one sending it to yourself. Filing a self-lawsuit to settle a canteen debt is the peak of professional dedication. #Bureaucracy #OfficeHumor #PaperworkLife (satire)
igHook: Tag someone whose filing system is so complex they've started auditing themselves.
imagePrompt: A cramped, dusty office desk covered in stacks of yellowing legal files and folders, with a single steaming cup of tea resting on a pile of stamped official documents.

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 3 wins by focusing on a self-contained, absurdly relatable micro-bureaucracy loop (suing oneself for a canteen bill) rather than relying on the overused trope of 'accidentally emailing the entire government' that cluttered several other candidates. It maintains a perfect deadpan tone, avoids AI-filler, and creates a specific, warm, and highly visual image of a clerk professionally processing his own samosa debt.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses a generic, common name (Ramesh Kumar) and describes a whimsical, self-contained satirical scenario about bureaucratic inefficiency. It does not target any specific real individual or public figure, and the image prompt is entirely generic.
